newsitem.title: USA: Chubb shares drop as Q3 results disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Chubb shares drop as Q3 results disappoint.

text.p: Chubb Corp shares fell about seven percent on Thursday after the company reported disappointing third quarter earnings, hurt by sharply higher catastrophe losses.
Premium growth also was slower than expected and helped drive down the price of the shares, analysts said.
Chubb reported third quarter earnings of $0.93 a share compared to Wall Street's consensus estimate of $0.98 a share.
Catastrophe losses were $23.9 million in the third quarter compared to $6.0 million in the 1995 third quarter.
"The whole nickel (shortfall), the difference is higher storm-related losses in the personal lines business in the third quarter," Lehman analyst Peter Wade said.
But, he said, "the things that are really driving the stock down are the (disappointing) top line."
"People were looking for a little bit of a recovery in the top line and didn't get it," he said.
Chubb shares fell 3-1/2, or more than seven percent, to close at 45-1/2.
Chubb was holding a conference call with analysts at 1600 EDT/2000 GMT to discuss the results.
Analysts speaking before the conference call said Chubb apparently chose to restrain growth amid intense competition that was driving prices down to unattractive levels.
Chubb Corp chief executive Dean O'Hare said competitive market conditions constrained commercial lines growth in the United States.
"We chose to protect profitability and still achieved good growth led by our specialty lines, particularly executive protection and financial institutions," O'Hare said in a statement.
Property-casualty net premiums written in the third quarter grew 6.1 percent to $1.2 billion. In the first nine months, net premiums written increased 10.3 percent to $3.6 billion.
For the year to date, about one-third of the premium growth was due to changes in the quota share reinsurance agreements with the Sun Alliance Group Plc.
These changes resulted in Chubb retaining a greater portion of its business written directly while assuming less reinsurance from Sun Alliance, Chubb said.
Changes in certain casualty reinsurance programs also contributed to premium growth in 1996.
"Personal lines experienced strong growth in the U.S. and we continued to build a base for future business in selected European markets," O'Hare said.
"Commercial lines growth in the U.S. was constrained by competitive market conditions," he said.
Chubb third quarter earnings shortfall follows a disappointing second quarter and a first quarter that was hit hard by catastrophes.
In the second quarter, operating earnings fell short of expectations and slowing premium growth emerged as a concern. The life insurance business also turned in weak results.
And in the first quarter, operating earnings came in just shy of the consensus estimate and declined compared to previous year. Catastrophic losses were $0.53 a share compared to $0.05 in 1995.

O'Hare said the company was pursuing an aggressive program to develop global property and casualty accounts, particularly among U.S.-based middle-market companies. This segment, O'Hare said, has been expanding rapidly overseas.
Chubb said its property and casualty business contributed $145.8 million to operating income in the 1996 third quarter, up from $139.9 million in 1995.
The combined loss and expense ratio was 97.2 percent for the quarter compared to 96.9 percent a year ago.
The combined ratio indicates whether a company is earning a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.
Life and health insurance income after taxes amounted to $10.6 million for the third quarter compared to $9.4 million a year ago.
